## Claims
- [source-backed] For bigrassmannian \(v=v_{r,s,t,n}\) with \(\mathfrak S_v=s_{i^j}\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), the two Schur intervals generate \(J_v\), and each has \(\binom{a+b}{a}\) elements. [source-2, lines 1382-1421]
- [proved] In the square family \(n=4m,\ r=n-r=2m,\ i=j=m\), one has \(a=b=m\) and the generator count is \(\binom{2m}{m}\). Thus \(m=1\) gives two-element sets \(\{s_1,s_2\}\) and \(\{s_1,s_{11}\}\); \(m=2\) gives six-element sets \(\{s_{22},s_{32},s_{33},s_{42},s_{43},s_{44}\}\) and \(\{s_{22},s_{221},s_{2211},s_{222},s_{2221},s_{2222}\}\). [source-2, lines 1394-1421, 1508-1515]
- [source-backed] These \(m=1,2\) cases lie in the authors’ reported finite verification range \(r\le4,\ n-r\le5\), so they support, but do not prove, minimality. [source-2, lines 1501-1502]
- [proved] The next square case \(m=3\) has \(n=12,\ r=n-r=6,\ i=j=3,\ a=b=3\), hence two generating sets of \(20=\binom63\) elements. It lies outside the reported verification range; its minimality remains conjectural. [source-2, lines 1394-1421, 1501-1502, 1508-1515]
- [proved] The general assertion that all inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets have a common cardinality is false under the stated graded-algebra hypotheses: let \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[x]/(x^2,6x)\), \(\deg x=1\), and \(M=(x)\). Then \(\Lambda_+M=0\), while both \(\{x\}\) and \(\{2x,3x\}\) are inclusion-minimal homogeneous generating sets of \(M\), of sizes \(1\) and \(2\); indeed \(x=2(2x)-3x\), whereas neither \(2x\) nor \(3x\) alone generates \(x\). This obstructs deriving common cardinality merely from the graded Nakayama criterion. [source-2, lines 1517-1534]
- [conjectural] Freeness \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\), if established, would rule out the preceding torsion obstruction and imply irredundance of either displayed family. The source records this only as a suspected statement. [source-2, lines 1536-1552]

## Strategy
Use the square family to separate:
1. source-reported supporting cases \(m=1,2\);
2. the first unreported case \(m=3\);
3. the algebraic torsion obstruction to arguments based solely on inclusion-minimal spanning sets.

## Gaps
No computation artifact or independent-review record was supplied. The source’s finite verification is evidence only, and neither it nor the examples proves the conjecture beyond its stated range.

## Next
Compute \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\) integrally for the \(m=3\) case, including torsion, to test whether \(20\) indecomposables are required.
